objectives: Turn Product and market compliance before ordering into concrete, measurable decisions that can be applied to a real store.

blocks.text: Identify customs code, restrictions, standards, labeling, safety, importer responsibility, and evidence for the destination market before paying for tooling. A sound decision always connects the customer need, the visual or commercial rule, its implementation in the site, and an observable signal. This prevents vague preferences and copied tactics whose purpose is not understood.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Product and market compliance before ordering is like arranging a physical shop: every color, space, message, or offer should help a visitor understand where they are, what they can buy, and why they can trust the next step.

Identify customs code, restrictions, standards, labeling, safety, importer responsibility, and evidence for the destination market before paying for tooling. Name the precise problem before selecting a tool. Observe context, device, intent, and customer objections. Then write a hypothesis that links one change to an expected result without presenting that hypothesis as established fact.

To master Product and market compliance before ordering, first build a minimal version with explicit rules, then inspect it on mobile and desktop. Contrast normal, empty, long, and error cases. Quality comes from a coherent testable system, not from accumulating visual effects or promotional messages.

This lesson delivers a compliance dossier tied to the exact product and country. It must record the starting situation, decision, expected evidence, and safety limit. Compare behavior and before/after metrics over enough time while accounting for traffic, costs, and satisfaction.

lessons.title: Customs, landed cost, inventory, and risk plan
prerequisites: Complete the web foundations or know how to open the project, edit a file, and verify the result in a browser. No previous commercial experience is required.
objectives: Turn Customs, landed cost, inventory, and risk plan into concrete, measurable decisions that can be applied to a real store.
Turn a landed-cost calculation and supply-chain risk register into concrete, measurable decisions that can be applied to a real store.

Turn Add product, packaging, inspection, freight, insurance, duties, tax, brokerage, delivery, finance, damage, and returns; include time buffer and fallback. into concrete, measurable decisions that can be applied to a real store.

blocks.text: Add product, packaging, inspection, freight, insurance, duties, tax, brokerage, delivery, finance, damage, and returns; include time buffer and fallback. A sound decision always connects the customer need, the visual or commercial rule, its implementation in the site, and an observable signal. This prevents vague preferences and copied tactics whose purpose is not understood.

blocks.title: Simple analogy
blocks.text: Customs, landed cost, inventory, and risk plan is like arranging a physical shop: every color, space, message, or offer should help a visitor understand where they are, what they can buy, and why they can trust the next step.

Add product, packaging, inspection, freight, insurance, duties, tax, brokerage, delivery, finance, damage, and returns; include time buffer and fallback. Name the precise problem before selecting a tool. Observe context, device, intent, and customer objections. Then write a hypothesis that links one change to an expected result without presenting that hypothesis as established fact.

To master Customs, landed cost, inventory, and risk plan, first build a minimal version with explicit rules, then inspect it on mobile and desktop. Contrast normal, empty, long, and error cases. Quality comes from a coherent testable system, not from accumulating visual effects or promotional messages.

This lesson delivers a landed-cost calculation and supply-chain risk register. It must record the starting situation, decision, expected evidence, and safety limit. Compare behavior and before/after metrics over enough time while accounting for traffic, costs, and satisfaction.
